record.original_question: What is the computational complexity of deciding ground reducibility for a finite term-rewriting system R and a term t, where t is ground reducible when every ground, variable-free instance of t contains a redex; in particular, can the known general and left-linear upper and lower bounds be improved?

evidence.quote: What is the complexity of deciding ground-reducibility?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let R be a finite term-rewriting system over a fixed finite signature, and let t be a term (possibly containing variables) over the same signature. Call t ground reducible by R if every ground instance of t (i.e., every term obtained from t by substituting variable-free terms for its variables) contains a redex of R, meaning some subterm that matches the left-hand side of a rule in R via some substitution.

Determine the exact computational complexity of the decision problem: given (R, t), decide whether t is ground reducible by R. In particular:
(a) For arbitrary finite R, establish tight upper and lower complexity bounds.
(b) For the restricted class where R is left-linear (no variable occurs more than once on any left-hand side), establish tight upper and lower complexity bounds.
Can the previously known upper and lower bounds in either setting be improved?
artifact.status_search_result: The complexity of deciding ground reducibility for a finite term-rewriting system has been settled: Comon and Jacquemard proved that the problem is EXPTIME-complete in general. The EXPTIME upper bound is obtained via deterministic tree automata with disequality constraints, and EXPTIME-hardness is proved by reduction from emptiness of intersections of recognizable tree languages. This matches and tightens earlier bounds for left-linear and general cases.

status_evidence.title: Ground reducibility is EXPTIME-complete
status_evidence.snippet: Ground reducibility is EXPTIME-complete in the general case, with the upper bound proved via automata with disequality constraints and the lower bound via tree-language intersection emptiness.
status_evidence.claim: Deciding ground reducibility for finite term-rewriting systems is EXPTIME-complete.

status_evidence.title: Ground Reducibility is EXPTIME-complete (HAL)
status_evidence.snippet: Comon and Jacquemard establish EXPTIME-completeness of ground reducibility, providing matching upper and lower bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Matching EXPTIME upper and lower bounds are established.
